title: NSA Violation: OON Anesthesia Balance Billing at INN Hospital - Scenario 17
claim_description:
[ILLEGIBLE...]
I HAD A LAPAROSCOPIC CHOLECYSTECTOMY AT ST. JUDC MEDICAL CENTER, WHICH IS IN MY INSURANCE NETWORK THE SURGEON WAS ALSO IN-NETWORK. HOWEVER THE ANESTHESIOLOGIST (APEX ANESTHESIA GROUP) WAS OUT-OF-NETWORK. I NEVER CHOSE THEM — THEY WERE ASSIGNED IN THE OPERATING ROOM. MY EOB SHOWS APEX ANESTHESIA BILLED $2,800 FOR CPT 00790 (ANESTHESIA FOR INTRAPERITONEAL PROCEDURES). THE PLAN PAID $0 AND I AM BCING TOLD I OWC THE FULL $2,800 (DENIAL REASON: PR-242, SERVICES NOT PROVIDED BY NETWORK/PRIMARY CARC PROVIDERS). THE EOB LISTS TOTAL PATIENT RESPONSIBILITY AS $3,200 — $4OO FOR THE SURGERY AND $2,800 FOR ANESTHESIA
benchmark_policy_excerpt:
SECTION 8: FEDERAL NO SURPRISES ACT PROTECTIONS
Under the Federal No Surprises Act, if you receive emergency services or are treated by an out-of-network ancillary provider (such as an anesthesiologist, pathologist, or radiologist) at an In-Network facility, you cannot be balance billed. Your patient responsibility will be calculated based on the In-Network cost-sharing amounts.
ground_truth_rationale: Apex Anesthesia Group is an OON ancillary provider at an INN facility. Under 45 CFR § 149.410(b) of the No Surprises Act, balance billing is prohibited. Patient responsibility is capped at 20% of allowed amount ($400).
